Different realities are being created through inaction, eventually leading to Earth. According to Plato and Nostics, the essence is a multi-layered, multi-dimensional world we access constantly. The earth we perceive is just the outermost shell in this universe.

The purpose of life in this world, according to Plato, is to return to the monad. This concept forms the framework for many religions, including Hinduism and Buddhism, where Nirvana signifies the return to the monad. Knowledge pursuit, philosophy, and love are means to achieve this goal.

Dante adds that the monad is love, which emanates throughout the universe as a divine spark within us. Love allows us to connect with each other; the more we love, the closer we come to the monad. Thus, Plato advocates for pursuing knowledge, while Dante emphasizes loving others unconditionally.

The question then arises: why does evil exist? For Plato, this world is insignificant; focus on knowledge to reunite with the monad. Dante suggests that free will, granted by the monad, allows us to make choices, even if they lead to bad outcomes. The divine spark within us is love, and messengers like Plato and Dante remind us of this.

The powerful want to control Earth, making it as real as possible because their power stems from believing only the material world exists. Science validates this belief by negating the spiritual realm. Transgression aligns with certain forces in the universe, which include evil entities.
